title: "About Me"

I am a computational biologist working as a consultant with the Quintarelli Laboratory in Oncohematology at [Ospedale Pediatrico Bambino Gesù](https://www.ospedalebambinogesu.it/) (OPBG) in Rome, Italy.

My current work is in pediatric cancer genomics and CAR-T cell therapy development. I analyze long-read Nanopore whole genome sequencing (WGS) and bulk RNA-seq to characterize T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), covering structural variant and single nucleotide variant detection. I also work on therapeutic target discovery for rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) using single cell and bulk RNA-seq from patient derived xenograft models and patient cohorts, and on transcriptome profiling of armored CAR.GD2.mbIL15 T cells in a neuroblastoma model.

Alongside the analysis work, I built the laboratory's compute infrastructure. This included an on-premise Ubuntu cluster with a HyperQueue job scheduler and containerized scientific software, and a comparative evaluation of AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and GARR for genomic workloads that meet Italian and GDPR health data privacy requirements.

Previously I was a senior computational biologist on the Research Scientific Computing team at [Seattle Children's Research Institute](https://www.seattlechildrens.org/research/) (SCRI) in beautiful Seattle, WA. I led the data analysis strategy for projects across oncology, developmental biology, and infectious disease, developed and adapted scalable genomics data pipelines using [Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/) and [nf-core](https://nf-co.re/) tools, and provided guidance on utilizing the high performance compute (HPC) cluster to empower researchers to access the computational resources at SCRI.

Before that I supported pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) translational research studies from the National Cancer Institute's TARGET initiative using genomic and transcriptomic 'big data' from next generation sequencing at [Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (FHCC)](https://research.fredhutch.org/meshinchi/en.html).
